column2: You are looking for milk in a supermarket. Ask an employee where you can find it.
You are at a bakery counter. Politely tell the assistant that you would like two bread rolls.
You are about to pay at a shop. Ask whether paying by bank card is possible.
You are pointing to a bag with no price tag. Ask its price.
The item you tried on is too big. Politely ask the assistant whether they also have a smaller size.
A cashier offers you a shopping bag. Tell them that you do not need a bag.
You have paid for your shopping. Politely ask the cashier for the receipt.
You are comparing two sets of apples. Point to the less expensive ones and explain the price difference.
A shop assistant asks what you are looking for. Explain that you want a present for your girlfriend.
You have chosen an item in a shop. Tell the assistant you will take this one, and thank them.
Your teacher has explained something, but you have not understood it. Politely ask for the explanation again.
You are pointing to a question in an exercise. Tell your teacher that you do not understand it.
A word in your textbook is new to you. Ask your teacher what that particular word means.
Your teacher is speaking. Ask politely for permission to ask a brief question.
Your teacher asks whether your homework is finished. Explain that you have already done it.
You and your classmates must submit an assignment. Ask when your group has to hand it in.
Someone asks where your pen is. Explain that it is lying on the table.
A friend asks about tomorrow's plans. Tell them that you are going to school tomorrow.
You arrive late to class because your train is delayed. Explain both your lateness and its cause.
You would like a classmate to practise with you. Ask whether the two of you can practise together.
You are at a railway station, ready to travel. Ask which platform the train departs from.
You are unsure whether this is your interchange station. Ask whether you need to change trains here.
You are about to board a train. Check whether this particular train goes to Bruges.
You are at the ticket counter. Politely tell the assistant that you would like a ticket to Ghent.
A friend's train has not arrived yet. Ask what time the train arrives.
You see a seat that appears empty. Ask another passenger whether that seat is available.
Your train is delayed by ten minutes. Tell the person who is waiting for you about your train's delay.
You need to buy your train ticket. Ask someone where you can buy it.
You are travelling by bus and your stop is next. Tell another passenger where you are getting off.
Your luggage is difficult to manage. Politely ask another person to help you with it.
You are ready to leave home, but cannot find your keys. Ask where your keys are.
Someone phones and asks what you are doing right now. Explain that you are cooking.
You are leaving the house with a friend. Ask whether they have locked the door.
Your housemate asks whether the dishes still need doing. Explain that you have already done them.
The room needs fresh air. Ask someone to open the window.
You are identifying the cups on a table. Point to one and tell the person you are addressing that it belongs to them.
A colleague asks about your usual journey home. Explain that you cycle home after work.
Someone is looking for milk. Tell them that there is milk in the fridge.
Someone asks what you are doing in your bedroom. Explain that you are tidying it, putting things back in place.
It is time for a meal. Suggest that you and the person you are addressing eat together.
You meet someone who speaks Dutch. Explain that you speak a little Dutch.
You are struggling to follow someone because they speak quickly. Ask them to speak a little more slowly.
You greet a friend and want to know how they are doing. Ask them.
Someone asks which city you live in. Tell them that you live in Roeselare.
You are getting to know someone. Ask where they are originally from.
You want to arrange something with a friend tomorrow. Ask whether they have time tomorrow.
You were expected to come today, but cannot. Tell the other person you cannot come today.
You are arranging to meet a friend. Suggest meeting at three o'clock.
A friend asks how you feel. Explain that you are tired, but otherwise feel good.
Someone has helped you. Thank them specifically for that help, using informal address.
A man is anxious that he might lose his keys. Tell someone what he is worried about, rather than saying the keys are already lost.
You are at a currency exchange desk. Ask what the exchange rate is at the moment.
A cashier asks how you are paying. Explain that you are using your credit card.
You look outside and can hardly see through the fog. Describe how foggy it is.
You are recalling a past visit. Before the visitors arrived, you had already baked the bread. Explain what was already done.
A colleague asks what you are doing at work. Explain that you are checking the stock.
A friend is exhausted and reluctant to rest. Explain that resting is good for them.
You have discussed an issue with someone you address formally. Ask their opinion about that issue.
A woman has left, and you do not know her destination. Ask where she went.
Your colleague needs a report. Say that you will prepare one.
You are recalling a couple's earlier housing search. Explain that they were looking for an apartment at that time.
You are recounting a workday. Say that the meeting ended.
You and some friends have finished a conversation that lasted for hours. Tell someone about its length.
Someone you address formally is waiting for updates. Promise to keep that person informed.
Someone asks you the time. The clock shows 5:30. Tell them the time in Dutch.
A friend asks which kind of weather you enjoy. Say that you love sunny days.
A male colleague has finished reading the report. Tell someone that he is finished with that reading task.
A friend has a task coming up later. Ask whether they will need help.
You and your companion are enjoying a visit. Tell your host that both of you feel like staying.
You are recalling a shopping trip. Tell someone that a man bought a souvenir.
Your group is preparing for a trip. Say that you will check the weather together.
You recognise the person in front of you, but cannot remember their name. Explain what you have forgotten.
You are considering travelling somewhere on foot. Ask whether it is possible to walk there.
You are thirsty at a café. Politely ask for some water.
A colleague has raised a topic that you cannot deal with now. Say that you will return to that topic later.
You and another person have had coffee together. Tell a friend what the two of you drank.
Someone asks when a man left. Explain that his departure was one hour ago.
You are invited to go out, but staying home appeals to you more. Explain your preference.
You are recounting yesterday's tasks. Say that a woman cleaned the desk.
You heard something earlier that sounded a little odd. Describe how it sounded, without calling it completely incomprehensible.
You need medical assistance. Tell someone that you need a doctor.
You are offering support to a guest. Tell them to let you know if they need anything.
Your friends have already watched a particular film. Tell someone that they have seen it.
You are checking an arrangement and confirming its details. Tell your colleague what you are doing.
A female colleague is occupied with writing an email right now. Describe what she is busy doing.
Someone has just made a suggestion that you agree with. Tell them that you agree with it.
You are describing a habit from an earlier period of your life. Explain that you used to go to the cinema.
You are recounting a past trip. Explain that the people you are discussing left early.
A friend has made an excellent suggestion. Respond enthusiastically by calling it a great idea.
An idea might work, but nobody has tested it. Explain that trying it would be worthwhile.
You are discussing a task with colleagues. Ask whether your group can work together on it.
Several people are improving their drawing skills through practice. Tell someone what they are practising.
A woman phoned your friend earlier. Tell that friend that she called them.
You have returned from a social event. Tell a friend that you met new people there.
You can see that rain will start very soon. Tell the person beside you what is about to happen.
The responsibility for tidying a shared space belongs to a man. Tell someone what he is responsible for.
You are talking about an earlier café visit. Say that you drank a lemonade.
You are speaking affectionately to someone. Explain that thinking about them makes you smile.
Your phone battery is low. Explain that you need to charge your phone.
A classmate is struggling to understand something. Encourage them to keep trying until they understand it.
You have been given a task, but not its due date. Ask when the deadline is.
Your group has finished a discussion. Suggest scheduling a follow-up.
You are considering walking to a destination. Ask whether it is a long walk, rather than asking if walking is possible at all.
Someone asks where a building is. Explain that it is opposite the park.
A colleague asks how you cope with extended working days. Explain that you are used to working long hours.
You do not understand something your classmate knows. Ask them directly to explain it to you.
You are speaking formally to a traveller about an upcoming visit. Ask where they will be staying.
You are recounting hearing a story again. Explain that you had heard that story before that occasion.
You are unsure how to proceed. Ask another person what you should do.
A friend describes an appealing plan. Respond that the plan sounds great.
Your friend has already eaten. Ask where they ate.
You are recalling receiving a suggestion too late. Explain that your group had already made a choice before that moment.
You are ordering eggs at a counter. Ask for a quantity of twenty-four, using the Dutch word for a dozen.
The original deadline no longer works. Suggest that your group set a new deadline.
A document is elsewhere. Tell someone to arrange for it to be sent to you, rather than asking them to send it personally.
Someone asks what you would enjoy doing now. Explain that you feel like eating.
You and your colleagues have finished a discussion about the project. Tell someone what your group talked about.
You are speaking formally to someone in a neighbourhood. Ask whether they know this local area.
You are pleased with an achievement. Tell someone how proud you feel.
You see a friend occupied with an activity. Ask what they are doing right now.
Your holiday is still ahead of you. Tell someone that your group is eagerly anticipating it.
You are recalling a past departure. Before you left, you had already switched off the lights. Explain what was already done.
Someone needs directions. Tell them to walk along the street they are currently on.
You are pointing at something you want in a shop. Tell the assistant that you would like it.
You are at a hotel and need internet access. Ask whether free Wi-Fi is available.
Yesterday, you visited a restaurant and tried a new dish. You are telling a friend about the visit. Say what you tried.
You are seated at a restaurant and want to look at the dishes available. Politely ask to see the menu.
The place where you are feels very cold. Describe the temperature here.
You are looking back at a past review meeting. Explain that your group had finished the project early before that meeting took place.
Someone has done you a favour. Thank them warmly, using a conventional expression meaning thank you very much.
You are looking for the railway station. Ask a passer-by where it is.
You and a friend are considering what to do next. Suggest going to have a cup of coffee together.
You are recalling a man you saw earlier. Say that he seemed very happy, without claiming you know exactly how he felt.
You are describing earlier weather. Tell someone that there was a thunderstorm.
Your dining companion reaches for the bill, but you have paid it. Tell them what you have done.
A friend trains for a sport. Ask how often they train.
Your group will meet again at an agreed time. Say that you will discuss the matter then.
You would like to exercise with a friend. Suggest going for a run together.
A male shopkeeper is occupied with closing the shop right now. Tell someone what he is busy doing.
You and a partner are considering starting a shop, but have not decided. Explain the idea your group is considering.
You are showing someone a purchase. Explain that you bought this item yesterday.
You are arranging to see a friend. Ask whether the two of you can meet on Tuesday.
Someone asks how you felt earlier. Explain that you felt a little tired.
You are recalling a past request to write a letter. Explain that you had already written it before that request arrived.
You want to stay in touch with a new acquaintance. Ask whether you can have their phone number.
Someone does not know the route. Offer to show that person the way.
A man is unable to speak on the phone now. Tell the caller that he will call back later.
You need help finding the route. Politely ask someone to show you the way.
Someone has just come indoors. Ask whether it is cold outside.
An arrangement no longer fits your schedule. Ask whether your group can reschedule it.
You are recounting a past incident. A man concealed an object so your group could not find it. Explain what he did.
You are describing a woman you saw earlier. Say that she was wearing a scarf.
You have finished considering your options. Tell someone that you made a decision.
Your phone has no battery power left. Explain the problem, without saying the device is missing.
Several patients are going to sit in the waiting room until the doctor calls them. Explain their plan and when the waiting will end.
A woman has been offered an opportunity and is pleased about it. Tell someone how she feels about that opportunity.
You have brought a bag containing food, but cannot find it. Ask where that bag is.
You are recalling the first attempt to use something. Explain that it did not work on that first attempt.
An image is difficult to see clearly. Describe how blurry it is, rather than saying that you do not understand it.
A friend has brought an item you discussed earlier. Ask whether they bought it for you.
Someone asks how difficult this particular exercise is. Tell them it is very easy.
A group has planned its holiday departure for Friday. Tell someone when they are leaving on holiday.
Your classmate has a text in front of them. Ask them to read that text aloud to you.
You cannot navigate the area without a map. Explain that you need one.
Someone asks why your group has come here. Explain that you are here to play.
Someone asks about your hygiene routine. Explain that you wash your hands before every meal.
Your companion is checking whether you can leave now. Tell them that you are ready to go.
A male colleague occasionally arrives late because of traffic. Explain both the occasional lateness and its cause.
You are recalling a family's earlier plans. Explain that they wanted to move to a larger house.
You need to use the toilet in an unfamiliar building. Ask where it is.
You are confident about a woman's future medical career. Say that she will be a great doctor one day.
You are recalling yesterday evening. Describe the sunset as beautiful.
You are recounting how a group gave a presentation. Explain that they used the meeting room for it.
The results are not available yet. Tell someone that you will know them by Monday at the latest.
You and the person you are addressing will attend a wedding. Tell them that you will dance with them there.
You have something the other person needs. Explain that you want to send it to them.
Someone needs support with a future task. Promise, on behalf of your group, that you will help them.
Some people are already approaching. Tell someone that they are on their way, rather than saying they have arrived.
Someone expects you to make decisions about a place you are visiting. Explain that you are only a guest.
A friend has invited you to their party. Tell them that you will come.
Someone asks about the condition of a surface or object. Explain that it is very dirty.
Another person is holding an object you want. Tell them directly to give it to you.
You are telling someone about a reception you attended. Explain that you danced with your wife at that event.
You are describing an old habit your group no longer necessarily follows. Explain that you used to stay up late.
The temperature is dropping. Tell someone that it is getting cold, describing the change rather than only the current state.
You are talking about where your household lived during an earlier period. Explain that you lived in the city.
A woman has bought the tickets for an outing. Tell someone that she bought them.
Helping in this situation is not easy. Explain that helping is difficult, without saying it is impossible.
Someone asks what you are considering. Explain that you are thinking carefully about the name.
You and your companions watched a sunset earlier. Tell someone what your group watched.
Someone has a document that you need. Ask whether they will send it to you.
You are looking at the night sky. Describe the moon as bright.
You are recounting a woman's achievement. Explain that she received an award for her work.
Someone is eating breakfast and you want their opinion of the meal. Ask how it is.
You are recalling a past conversation about the news. Explain that you had already seen the news before that conversation.
Someone wants you to explain something, but you are unable to. Tell them that you cannot explain it to them.
Something has gone wrong and you are responsible. Admit that it is your fault.
You are recounting where you were earlier. Explain that you were standing and waiting at the bus stop.
A woman left her coffee untouched. Tell someone that she did not drink her coffee.
You are checking on a friend right now. Ask whether they are sleeping at this moment.
You are recounting a shopping trip. Say that you bought some fruit.
A group is discussing the finer points of an arrangement right now. Tell someone what they are talking about.
You are looking for a bed in a place you do not know. Ask where the bed is.
Someone has an object that belongs to your group. Tell that person to give it back to all of you.
Someone asks which airline your group uses. Explain that you fly with the same airline every time.
Someone asks for information you cannot share at this point. Explain that you cannot tell them yet.
A group is considering a house move, but has not decided. Explain what they are thinking about doing.
You are pointing to a place some distance away. Explain that the thing someone is looking for is over there.
You need to communicate with someone you address formally. Ask whether they speak English.
You are recalling a group's earlier discussion. Explain that they made plans for the weekend.
The person you are addressing needs to pay attention to what is said. Tell them that they need to listen.
You are describing what a group was doing at an earlier moment. Explain that they were watching the match.
A man is occupied with cleaning the windows right now. Describe what he is busy doing, rather than saying he is tidying a room.
Someone asks whether an object or surface is dirty. Tell them that it is clean.
Someone has arrived at a place you are discussing. Ask who is there now.
Someone asks whose bag this is. Point to it and explain that it belongs to you.
You are recounting a request your group received earlier. Explain that the other people asked your group to come early.
You are recalling a walk or journey with your companions. Explain that your group passed the bank.
A friend thinks they lost the match, but that is not what happened. Tell them they did not lose it.
You are recounting how some people bought furniture. Explain that they paid for the furniture in cash.
Someone asks what you hear in the mornings. Explain that you hear the birds singing every morning.
The same music has become tiresome to you. Explain that you are fed up with this music.
You are discussing a man's car. Tell someone that you like his car.
You are describing a habit from an earlier period of your life. Explain that you used to go to the park.
Someone asks about your daily learning. Explain that you learn something new every day.
A woman is going to develop more confidence in herself. Explain this expected change in her self-belief.
You are recounting how a woman felt after sleeping. Say that she woke up and felt much better.
Someone asks you to describe a man's height. Explain that he is very tall.
Someone asks about a man's usual laundry arrangements. Explain that he washes his clothes at the laundrette.
Friends are considering activities to do together. Describe bowling as a fun social activity.
You are telling someone about a phone call you received earlier today. Explain that a man called you this morning.
You are leaving briefly and expect to return very soon. Reassure the other person that you will be right back.
Someone asks how a man normally travels to work. Explain that he goes by bus.
A woman loves singing above other activities. Tell someone that singing is her passion.
Your group is ready to leave. Tell the person staying behind that you are leaving now.
A woman is singing at this very moment. Describe what she is doing now.
Someone asks about drawing as a pastime. Describe it as a creative hobby.
Someone wants to know the size of an object you are discussing. Say that you will measure it.
Another person has something you want to see. Ask whether they will show it to you.
A woman enjoys preparing food for her friends. Explain that she likes cooking for them, rather than only saying she can cook.
Someone thinks they must stay, but they are permitted to leave. Tell that person that they are free to go.
You are recounting an earlier delay. A woman spent one hour sitting and waiting in the restaurant. Explain what she did and for how long.
You are telling someone about help you received earlier. Say that a man gave you good advice.
You are getting to know someone and discussing employment. Ask where they work.
Another person needs an object lifted. Say that you will lift the object you are discussing.
Someone is deciding whether to help. Explain that helping is the better choice.
You want to know the current weather conditions. Ask what the weather is like.
Your group needs water and you do not know who has any. Ask whether anyone has water.
You understand something now because a woman explained it to you. Tell someone that she explained it to you.
You are recalling a woman looking upwards earlier. Say that she was looking at the sky.
You want to know the cost of an item you are discussing. Ask what the price is.
You are considering an activity or place. Ask whether it is safe.
A colleague asks how your group handles problems. Explain that you solve them as soon as they arise.
You are introducing your husband to another person. Identify him as your husband.
Someone asks about a man's eating habits. Explain that he follows a healthy diet.
Several people are discussing a film right now. Tell someone what they are talking about.
Someone asks what makes you impatient. Explain that you lose your patience when people are rude.
You are worried about what lies ahead. Tell someone that you are afraid of the future.
You can see that something is wrong, but do not know what. Ask what the problem is.
Someone asks about your morning routine. Explain that you stand at the bus stop every morning.
You expect a woman to find a new job before long. Tell someone what she is going to find soon.
You are recounting a woman's absence from class. Explain that she did not go to school.
You are recalling an old summer tradition. Explain that your group used to go to the beach every summer.
Someone asks for an answer that is difficult to give. Explain that it is hard to say.
You are recalling a past visit. Your group had already cleaned the house before the visitors arrived. Explain what was already done.
You are recalling being asked to check the time. Explain that you had already checked it before that request.
You are looking at an object whose appearance resembles gold. Describe the resemblance without claiming that it is real gold.
Your household divides its chores. Explain that walking the dog is your responsibility.
Construction has not started yet. Explain that the people you are discussing will start building the new building next month.
Someone is worried about the condition they left something in. Reassure them that they did not make a mess of it.
A friend was feeling unwell earlier. Ask whether they are feeling better now.
A group has training still to attend. Predict that they will understand the rules after that training.
You are waiting for a service and need to plan your time. Ask how long the wait is.
Someone asks whether you need anything. Explain that you are thirsty.
You are recounting how a woman learned some news. Explain that she heard the news on the radio.
You cannot pay without the wallet you have misplaced. Explain that you need your wallet.
You are describing a group's situation at a past moment. Explain that they did not have any water.
A group plans to put up decorations later today. Explain that they will hang them up this afternoon.
Your attempt has failed, but you are going to make another attempt. Tell the other person you will try again.
A woman plans to travel to London by plane next summer. Tell someone about her travel plan.
You used to know the answer to a question, but cannot remember it now. Explain both the earlier knowledge and the present forgetting.
A colleague asks about your group's regular writing tasks. Explain that you write reports every week.
Some people have not arrived yet. Ask when they will arrive.
You are considering a different job, without having decided. Explain that you are thinking about changing jobs.
You hear a noise you cannot identify. Ask what that sound is.
A group has left and you do not know the destination. Ask where they went.
Someone is about to go out, but their room needs tidying first. Tell them they are going to tidy it before leaving.
You are recalling how a woman appeared earlier. Say that she seemed confused, without claiming certainty about her thoughts.
Someone asks about the vegetables your household eats. Explain that you grow your own vegetables in the garden.
You are discussing your old car. Explain that you sold it last month.
Someone has told you what happened, but not the reason. Explain that you want to know why.
You are recounting a group's arrival at an earlier event. Explain that they arrived late.
You are recalling a past request to do the shopping. Explain that you had already done it before that request.
Something belonging to the person you are addressing needs repair. Offer to repair it for them.
Summer is nearly over and autumn is approaching. Tell someone that autumn is coming.
You are describing where a man usually stands at the bakery. Explain that he is behind the counter.
Someone asks about your daily work schedule. Explain that you start work at eight in the morning.
Someone has just thanked you. Respond with the usual polite expression meaning they are welcome.
Someone asks about your morning household routine. Explain that you make your bed every morning.
Some people are using paint left over from another task. Explain that they are using that paint for the bedroom.
You are speaking formally to someone beside a desk. Ask whether this is their workplace.
Your team needs an agenda for a meeting. Offer to prepare the agenda yourself.
A task has been proposed without explaining its purpose. Ask what the goal is.
You are recalling a completed discussion with colleagues. Explain that your group discussed many things.
You have arrived somewhere and are pleased to be there. Express that it is nice to be here.
Some people's opinions are being overlooked. Suggest that your group make those people's voices heard.
You and the person you are addressing met yesterday morning. Remind them when the two of you met.
Your group has received a contract. Suggest looking it over together, without saying you have approved it.
Your group has not chosen a solution yet. Explain that you are considering all the options.
Someone asks about your training. Explain that you have completed it.
A man must approve something before you can proceed. Explain that you need his approval.
Another person is holding a report belonging to a man. Tell them directly to give that man his report.
You are recounting a woman's help during an earlier journey. Explain that she explained the route.
Someone asks who an item was bought for. Explain that your group bought it for a woman.
An explanation is not detailed enough for you. Politely ask the person, using formal address, to explain this further.
Your team needs its available resources assigned to tasks. Say that you will allocate the resources.
You are talking about a man's work yesterday evening. Explain that he worked late that evening.
Another person has an item you need. Tell them that they should bring it to you, giving advice rather than a bare command.
Someone asks what you are doing right now. Explain that you are making a phone call.
Someone wants an explanation, but now is not a good time. Tell them you will explain it later.
Someone hopes to build a future without much effort. Explain that building a future takes work.
Your colleague asks about the proposal you were preparing. Tell them that your proposal is ready.
You need someone to deal with a matter and bring it to completion. Politely ask, using formal address, whether they can handle it.
A man is occupied with repairing a leak right now. Tell someone what he is busy doing.
You have an idea to contribute to a discussion. Ask permission to suggest something.
Someone asks why you cannot work as usual. Tell them that you are ill.
You are discussing the computer network's upkeep. Explain that it needs maintenance on a regular basis.
Someone asks what you are doing with your old laptop. Tell them that you are selling it.
You have just explained something to another person. Ask whether it is clear.
Someone has agreed to attend an event. Tell them directly to show up, without adding a new time or place.
You are discussing a particular investment. Warn that this investment is very risky.
You are identifying who makes a payment to a woman. Tell the person you are addressing that they pay it to her.
You have arrived thirty minutes before the meeting starts. Explain that you are half an hour too early for it.
Someone asks who an item was made for. Explain that a man made it for your group.
You are pointing to a particular folder. Tell someone to give this folder to the manager.
Your presentation has not begun yet, but you are prepared. Explain that you are ready for your presentation.
A colleague is at a desk. Ask whether they are writing the report right now.
Someone wants to tell you something before the meeting. Ask whether they have to tell you that before the meeting.
You are discussing forms and need just one of them. Explain that you need one, referring back to the forms without repeating the noun.
You see a situation in which someone needs to take action. Tell another person directly to intervene.
Someone has suggested a workable plan. Respond that their suggestion sounds like a plan.
A person's explanation is too abstract. Politely ask them, using formal address, to give examples.
Some visitors have left and are no longer here. Tell someone that they are gone.
You want a written price quotation from a supplier. Politely ask them to draw one up.
A colleague asks what your team offered a woman. Explain that your team offered her your services.
Someone is unsure which form to complete. Point to one and tell them to use this form.
Your group's current approach is inadequate. Explain that you need a new strategy.
Another team has a meeting room that your group would like to use. Ask whether your group can use their room.
You are showing something your group leaves behind for future generations. Describe it as your group's legacy.
A colleague was responsible for a task. Ask whether they have finished their task.
You need to check a woman's appointments. Say that you will check her calendar.
Your group has nearly finished a proposal. Suggest finalising your group's proposal together.
You are recounting a past request to phone the office. Explain that you had already called the office before that request.
Someone asks about the project your group is working on. Describe your project as challenging.
A man is occupied with putting goods into a truck right now. Explain what he is busy doing.
You need an access code. Ask a colleague, using informal address, to tell you the code.
Some documents are missing. Tell another person directly to find the missing documents.
There are new safety rules you do not understand. Ask a colleague to explain those rules to you.
A woman explains things well. Tell someone about her skill at explaining things.
Someone is keeping a concern to themselves. Politely ask them, using informal address, to talk with you about it.
You have to ask someone an uncomfortable question. Express that you are sorry to have to ask it.
A woman has returned your badge to you. Tell someone what she gave back to you.
You are pointing to a package that must go to reception. Tell someone to take this package there.
You are preparing for this afternoon's meeting. Ask what the agenda is for this afternoon.
A product is out of date. Explain that the product needs an update.
Someone has a problem that you can handle. Offer to take care of it.
You are speaking formally to a specialist about a network problem. Ask whether they can provide a solution to this problem.
Someone you address formally doubts the value of their contribution. Explain that their input is crucial.
A trade fair is taking place next week. Tell someone that you want to go to it next week.
A colleague asks what you are doing with a package. Explain that you are weighing the package.
You are testing an audio connection with someone. Ask whether they can hear you.
A man leads a team that has a great deal to do. Tell someone that his team is very busy.
An upcoming event has already been mentioned. Say that you are looking forward to it, without naming the event again.
Someone is concerned that a proposal might bother you. Reassure them that you do not mind.
You are discussing another group's ideas. Describe their ideas as innovative.
A task has just been agreed. Tell your colleague you will begin working on it immediately.
You are recalling a man's work being acknowledged by others. Explain that his efforts were recognised, without naming who recognised them.
Your group cannot finish within the time available. Explain that you need more time.
Some people are discussing how much something costs right now. Tell someone what they are talking about.
Someone has completed a task successfully. Congratulate them with a short expression meaning well done.
A woman sent photos to your group earlier. Tell someone what she sent to you.
Someone asks whether you are certain about a matter already discussed. Explain that you are not sure yet.
An offer seems unusually attractive. Ask what hidden disadvantage or catch there is.
You are recounting a man's earlier conversation. Explain that he spoke with the manager.
Your group has too much work concentrated on a few people. Suggest delegating tasks.
You are recounting a man's completed work. Explain that he finished his task.
You need to find the person responsible for leading an activity. Ask who is in charge.
You have a signed contract that must reach a man. Tell someone to send the signed contract to him.
You are dealing with a particular leak. Explain that you have to find a solution to this leak.
Someone asks why you have come here. Explain that you are here to ask for advice.
A colleague asks what is occupying you today. Explain that you are busy with the planning today.
Someone needs to pay close attention to spoken information. Tell them directly to listen carefully.
Your group needs another group's input before Friday. Tell a colleague what you need and when you need it.
Someone asks why you are keeping your phone close. Explain that you are waiting for a phone call.
Several people are improving their abilities through practice. Describe them as practising their skills.
Your group is considering finalising an agreement. Ask whether you can close this deal.
Your group is ready to begin a presentation. Suggest starting the presentation together.
You are describing a vision agreed by your group. Identify it as your shared vision.
You meet a friend and want to know how their work is going. Ask about their work.
A technician needs a spare battery. Tell someone to give the spare battery to the technician.
Someone has told you bad news. Express that you are sorry to hear that.
A man informed your group that the train is delayed. Tell someone what he told you, keeping the train's delay as current information.
You are discussing how fast something is moving. Ask what its speed is.
Someone needs a particular answer. Tell them to find the answer in the manual.
You are ready to send an email you wrote. Tell someone that you will send your email.
Someone asks about acting as a career. Describe it as a demanding profession.
You borrowed a key from the person you are addressing and have returned it. Tell them what you gave back.
A woman speaks knowledgeably about a topic. Explain that she knows what she is talking about.
A point needs more explanation. Politely ask the person, using formal address, to clarify that in more detail.
Some things have been used up. Ask what remains, without assuming a particular quantity is left.
A man now has the opportunity he has been waiting for. Tell someone that his time has come, in this positive opportunity sense.
A new scanner is available. Explain that you want to use the new scanner.
Someone makes a useful observation during a discussion. Respond that it is a good point.
Some experienced people could train a man. Ask whether they can teach him how to operate the machine.
Your team is deciding how to use its available money. Speaking for the team, explain that you are planning your budget.
Some people taught you to fasten a safety belt. Explain what they taught you how to do.
Some people are tidying up and need assistance. Tell another person to help them with that activity.
You are discussing a special strength that gives your group an advantage. Ask what your group's secret weapon is, figuratively.
Your group has arrived after the agreed time. Speaking for the group, explain that you are late.
A man wants to buy an old printer that your colleague can sell. Tell your colleague directly to sell the old printer to him.
You are evaluating training a man received earlier. Explain that his training was effective.
Someone asks how hard it is to operate a business. Explain that running a business is difficult.
You need an invitation written. Ask a colleague informally to write the invitation for you.
Someone asks about the current economy. Explain that it is growing.
A meeting was scheduled, but its cancellation is now confirmed. Tell someone that the meeting has been cancelled.
Some people intend to remain late, but have not done so yet. Explain their plan.
You need a colleague's attention now. Ask informally whether they are available at this moment.
Your group is considering a different menu, without having decided. Explain that you are thinking about changing the menu.
Someone knows about an event your group wants to hear about. Tell that person to tell your group about it.
Someone has given you advice. Explain that you appreciate their advice, using informal address.
A colleague asks how your group views its customers. Explain that your customers are important.
You are recalling a past reminder to send a letter. Explain that you had already sent the letter before that reminder.
You are discussing spare keys. Explain that you have three of them, referring back to the keys without repeating the noun.
A malfunction threatened the schedule, but the team met its deadline. Explain both the success and the obstacle it overcame.
Someone asks whether you are certain about a claim. Explain that you are not sure about that claim.
You are recounting where a man was at an earlier moment. Explain that he was not at the desk, rather than describing an ongoing activity.
A lamp is broken and you are attempting a repair. Explain that you are trying to repair the broken lamp, without claiming success yet.
Someone asks how difficult a particular program is to learn. Explain that this program is easy to learn.
Something is broken and you are comparing two options. Ask which is better: repairing it or replacing it.
Someone asks about the duration of a discussion. Explain that the discussion is very short.
You are recalling a customer's arrival after closing time. Explain that your group had already closed the shop before that arrival.
You are recounting the outcome of another group's proposal. Explain that their proposal was accepted, without naming who accepted it.
A colleague may already have shown you a new design. Ask whether they have shown it to you.
Someone is about to leave, but a task must be done first. Tell them to do this before leaving.
You are recalling a past financial review. Explain that your group had already closed the financial year before that review began.
Someone asks what you are considering. Explain that you are thinking carefully about the goal.
Someone asks whether you will change position. Say that you will remain standing here.
A group is discussing the quality of an item, rather than its colour. Tell someone which subject they are discussing and which they are not.
Someone has an item you want to inspect briefly. Ask them to let you have a quick look.
You are discussing your company's values. Explain that your company values diversity.
Someone asks whose computer that is. Point to it and explain that it belongs to a man already mentioned.
You want a brief conversation with a colleague. Ask informally whether they can talk for a moment.
A woman has a new job and is pleased with it. Tell someone how she feels about her new job.
You received an email from a man earlier. Tell someone that he sent you an email.
Some people have written a letter to the person you are addressing. Tell that person what they have written to them.
Someone is discussing the cost of shopping. Explain that buying clothes is expensive.
A group will telephone someone as soon as an order is ready. Tell that person, using formal address, when the group will call them.
A man gave feedback earlier. Ask what his feedback was.
You are speaking formally during an online meeting. Politely tell another participant to share their screen.
A woman returned a refundable deposit to your group. Tell someone what she returned to you.
Someone asks who is responsible for a particular duty. Identify it as your responsibility.
A report needs to be sent. Tell your colleague that you will send the report.
You are discussing a particular measurement. Ask how reliable this measurement is.
A colleague is discouraged. Explain that remaining positive is important.
You see a colleague preparing for something. Ask informally whether they are busy with the preparation.
You are recalling a man's explanation. Explain that he explained his theory.
You have completed some work and want it checked. Politely tell the person, using formal politeness, to check your work.
There is time to speak now, but the meeting starts shortly. Tell someone to talk now and give that reason.
A man is deciding what strategic action to take. Ask what his next move is.
A man is due to arrive. Ask what time he arrives.
Your group faces competition and cannot afford to lose its competitive position. Explain that you have to remain competitive.
You are organising something for the neighbourhood. Say that you will send an invitation to all the neighbours.
Several people are waiting patiently through a delay. Describe them as exercising patience.
One man will explain a diversion route to another man. Tell someone who will explain it and to whom.
A man is expected at an entrance. Tell another person directly to wait for him by the entrance.
Someone is concerned you will be late. Promise them that you will be on time.
You and a friend have arranged to meet tomorrow by the stop. Tell that friend when and where you will see them.
You are carrying too much. Politely tell someone to carry the folders for you.
Someone asks why you have come to the site. Explain that you are here to work on the renovation project.
Someone is installing a program. Tell them to start this program after the installation.
A group is concentrating on its work. Explain what they are focusing on.
You are recounting why a man departed early. Explain that he left early because the train was cancelled.
Several approaches have been proposed. Ask which approach is best.
A zip is broken and you intend to repair it. Tell someone what you are going to repair.
Your group needs to assess how far it has got. Suggest reviewing your progress together.
A colleague has announced a decision. Ask whether this is their own decision, using informal address.
A man is occupied with checking the time right now. Describe what he is doing.
A colleague suggested an idea earlier and you liked it. Tell that colleague how you felt about their idea.
You are speaking formally to a guest about their reservation. Politely tell them to confirm their booking.
Your group has not made an investment decision yet. Explain that you are considering the risk of this investment.
You work for a small company. Ask what advantage your company has compared with larger companies.
Someone has proposed a solution, but it has not been tested. Ask whether this solution will work.
Your group cannot resolve a conflict alone. Explain that you need your manager to resolve this conflict.
Your group has achieved a shared goal. Suggest celebrating your group's success.
Something being discussed matters greatly to how your group works together. Explain its importance for your cooperation.
Your group needs to understand how some materials differ. Tell a specialist to explain the difference between these materials to your group.
A colleague was repairing your bicycle for you. Ask whether they have repaired it for you.
You are deciding whether to wait for a repair. Ask whether the repair will take a long time.
The customer has signed off the final design. Tell someone that the customer has approved the final design.
You are recounting a man's completed task. Explain that he finished the work.
A colleague thinks they made a mistake, but you have checked their work. Reassure them that they have not made a mistake.
A woman needs to be contacted later. Tell another person to call her after lunch.
A man is due to attend a meeting shortly. Tell someone that his meeting starts soon.
You hear that someone is telephoning. Ask who is calling.
Your group has completed a learning activity. Ask what the most important insights are.
You need to know the date for registration. Ask what the registration date is.
You need an invoice from a colleague. Ask whether they have sent you the invoice.
A chair is damaged and you want to repair it. Explain that you want to repair the damaged chair.
Several people are exchanging ideas. Explain that they share their ideas.
You do not understand a procedure already mentioned. Politely ask someone, using formal address, to guide you through it.
A supervisor was evaluating a man's work. Politely ask whether they have assessed his work.
Someone you address formally has waited patiently during a delay. Thank them specifically for their patience while waiting.
A man needs a train ticket, but cannot buy it himself. Tell another person to buy the ticket for him.
A woman has presented your idea as her own. Tell someone that she has stolen your idea.
You are recounting a man's effort on a task. Explain that he worked very hard.
You are talking to someone about how they looked earlier. Tell them that they looked very tired.
Some test samples need to reach a laboratory. Tell another person to take the samples to the laboratory.
You are starting a training course. Ask what the overall aim of this particular course is.
Your group must finish an activity before another appointment. Ask how much time your group has.
You are attending a session where device use may be restricted. Ask permission to use your laptop.

You are discussing a particular worktop. Explain that this worktop is easy to clean.
You are showing the agreed schedule for your group's training day. Identify it as your agenda for that day.
You are recalling where your group worked earlier. Explain that you worked at the office.
A colleague has explained their doubts to you. Tell them that you understand why they are unsure.
You are pointing to a cycle path protected from traffic. Describe this cycle path as very safe.
You are speaking formally to someone who may have written an accident report. Ask whether this is their report of the accident.
A man is selling his bicycle to several people. Explain what he is selling and to whom.
A friend will move home, but has not explained their arrangements. Ask what their plan is for the move.
You need a report that someone else has. Politely ask them, using formal address, to send you the report.
A group is struggling to find accommodation. Ask what their greatest obstacle is in finding housing.
You need to sign this form, but have no pen. Ask a person informally whether you may borrow their pen for that purpose.
You arrived after the final tram had departed. Explain that you are too late for the last tram.
Your group wants new ideas to develop. Explain that you have to encourage innovation.
Some bakers produce particularly good bread. Ask what their special strength or technique is when baking bread, using the secret-weapon metaphor.
A visitor wants coffee, but the machine is broken. Apologise and explain that the coffee machine is broken.
You are looking at a sequence of numbers. Ask what the next number is in this particular sequence.
Your group needs someone to organise transport and practical arrangements. Offer to handle the logistics.
You are applying for a permit and have completed one step. Ask what the next step is in the application process.
A language course has not started yet. Explain that your group is eagerly anticipating the start of that course.
You have arrived to fix a building's lift. Explain to someone that you are here to repair the lift.
This form requires very little time to complete. Tell someone that it can be filled in quickly.
Two people are expected to miss registration. Predict that they will be too late for registration.
Someone asks why you did not receive a delivery yourself. Explain that you were not at the office when it arrived.
Your group is choosing between acting now and waiting for confirmation. Explain that waiting for confirmation is better.
You cannot understand a letter. Politely ask someone informally to explain the content of this letter to you.
You live in Belgium and intend to continue living there. Explain your plan to remain living in Belgium.
Your neighbours want to organise a neighbourhood party. Suggest brainstorming ideas for that party together.
A disagreement is becoming heated. Explain that it is important to remain calm during a conflict.
You are showing someone a particular parking meter. Explain that this parking meter is easy to use.
Your group has separate objectives that must fit together. Explain that you have to align your goals with each other.
You are recounting a man's achievement. Explain that he completed his training without financial support.
You are discussing what worries you about attempting something important. Admit that you are afraid of failure.
You are discussing a particular difficult task during your internship. Identify it as your greatest challenge during the internship.
Your group is in a cold room and the heating is off. Explain that you have to turn on the heating.
People wonder whether your presence here is temporary. Reassure them that you are here to stay.
Your group has submitted a job application and is waiting hopefully. Explain that you are looking forward to the reply to your application.
The roof has a leak. Speaking for the people preparing a repair, promise that you will try to repair the leak in the roof.
You are writing a formal request to someone with an outdated task status. Politely tell them to update their status.
A man nearby knows the area. Tell a visitor to ask him for directions to the station.
You are speaking formally to a new participant. Ask what they expect from the experience.
A woman has prepared a proposal and can now explain it. Tell someone that she is ready to explain her proposal.
You are pointing out a matter that must be addressed at once. Explain that this requires immediate attention.
Someone has made commitments but has not fulfilled them. Tell them directly to keep their promises.
You have compared two versions and found no alteration. Tell the person who was editing it that they have not made a change.
You have just finished a job interview. Ask the interviewer what your next step is after this interview.
A task is difficult, but you are putting in your strongest effort. Reassure someone that you are doing your best.
You are discussing an earlier conversation. Explain that the people being discussed were not in the room during that conversation.
You are recalling a man's reaction to a completed task. Explain that he was happy with the result.
You lent some tools to the person you are addressing. Tell them to bring the borrowed tools back to you.
You cannot untie a particular knot. Ask someone what the trick is to loosening this knot.
Some customers are waiting for return calls. Explain that it is time to call the customers back.
A man has experience handling heavy items. Explain that he is used to heavy lifting, rather than saying he used to lift things in the past.
Some visitors have arrived to join a guided tour. Explain why they are here.
You have a possible business idea, but have not decided to act. Explain that you are thinking about starting a business.
You have bought a dictionary for the person you are addressing. Tell them what you bought for them.
Your group has spent more money than the budget allowed. Explain that you are over your budget.
You are watching a river whose water is getting higher. Tell someone that the water level is rising.
You are discussing an amount of paint and pointing at a wall. Explain that the paint is enough for this wall.
You are recalling a conference you attended with others. Explain that your group stayed at the hotel during the conference.
Someone called you, but there is no voicemail message. Tell that caller that they did not leave a message on your voicemail.
A designer has a new design to present to some people. Tell the designer to show them the new design.
You are preparing to do work in a library. Explain that you are going to work in the library, without saying it is your employer.
You and other learners are gathered for a cooking class that starts at this moment. Tell someone that your cooking lesson begins now.
A woman bought paint on behalf of your group. Tell someone what she bought for your group.
Your group has discussed several holiday periods without choosing. Suggest making a decision about the holiday dates together.
You must complete a form in blue ink and lack a suitable pen. Explain that you need a pen with blue ink.
A friend plans to move home next week, but their availability is uncertain. Ask whether they will be free next week to move house.
You are discussing the recipe for this particular soup. Explain that its recipe is simple.
Your group would like to volunteer, but has not identified suitable opportunities. Suggest identifying opportunities for volunteer work together.
You are recounting a technician's arrival. Explain that you had already done the preparatory work when the technician arrived.
A student is working at a desk. Ask whether they are currently working on the report about the excursion.
A friend has answered an invitation. Ask whether that is their final answer to the invitation.
You are looking for a man's office inside this building. Ask where his office is in this building.
You are inspecting a particular machine. Explain that maintaining this machine is important.
You missed a call from the dental practice while working. Explain that you will call the dentist back after work.
Your group has solved a storage difficulty. Explain that you have found a solution to the storage problem.
You need a bicycle shop on a Monday. Ask whether the bicycle shop is open on Mondays.
A company has finished revising its policy. Tell someone that the company has updated its policy.
A friend is about to book something. Encourage them to be sensible and compare prices before booking.
